Patient Roland Vickers, DOB 05/22/1940. Patient's son, Gideon, calling on his behalf, (404)-555-0164. Reported that his father's hip and back pain was worse and asked to increase his pain medicine.
  Caller: "His pain is worse. It's his hips, and his lower back."
  Explanation: Documents the pain concern prompting the call.

• Hip and lower back pain of about 5/10 had worsened over the last 3 days.
  Caller: "He says a five. Maybe a five. It was a three last week."
  Explanation: Documents pain severity and trend.
• Meth a dome 10 mg three times a day was reported (unclear; the name was also heard as methadone and was not confirmed), and the caller wanted to double the dose.
  Caller: "The meth a dome. Ten milligrams, three times a day."
  Explanation: Documents the current pain medication while preserving the unresolved name conflict.
• The caller wanted to double the dose because the pain was no longer controlled.
  Caller: "So I wanted to ask if I could give him more. Like double the meth a dome."
  Explanation: Documents the caller's request.
• He was sleeping most of the day, more than before.
  Caller: "He sleeps most of the day. More than before."
  Explanation: Documents increased sleepiness.
• His last bowel movement was yesterday morning and normal.
  Caller: "Yesterday morning. It was normal."
  Explanation: Documents a pertinent negative for constipation.
• Appetite was reduced, with a few bites at each meal.
  Caller: "He's eating a little. A few bites at each meal."
  Explanation: Documents decreased appetite.
• No vomiting was reported.
  Caller: "No. No vomiting."
  Explanation: Documents a pertinent negative.

  Nurse: "I can't change the dose over the phone."
  Explanation: Documents the medication safety instruction.
• Planned to message the hospice physician tonight to review the pain plan.
  Nurse: "I'm going to message our hospice doctor tonight, and ask him to review the pain plan."
  Explanation: Documents the planned physician notification.
• Planned to call back tomorrow morning with the doctor's answer.

  Explanation: Documents the planned callback.

• Advised giving the medicine exactly as labeled, writing down each dose and time, and never doubling up.
  Nurse: "please give exactly what the label says, and write down each dose and the time on a sheet. And never double up."
  Explanation: Documents medication-safety instructions.
• Advised calling right away if he became very sleepy, hard to wake, or his breathing slowed, and calling 911 if he could not be woken.
  Nurse: "If he gets very sleepy, hard to wake, or his breathing slows down, call me right away."
  Explanation: Documents return precautions and emergency instructions.
• Advised pillows under the hips, repositioning every 2 hours, and a warm pack on low.
  Nurse: "put pillows under his hips, change his position every two hours, and a warm pack on low, wrapped in a towel."
  Explanation: Documents comfort measures.
